title: Late Onset Myocarditis Following Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: A Case Series with Literature Review
content: It would be fair to say that immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy brought about a revolution in cancer treatment. However, it is important to note that ICI therapy can potentially lead to immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including myocarditis. While early-onset myocarditis is well-known, it is becoming increasingly recognized that late-onset cases may also occur. This case series presents four cases of late-onset ICI-associated myocarditis, which serve to underscore the importance of long-term surveillance for this potentially fatal complication. All patients presented with a variety of cardiac symptoms, including chest pain, shortness of breath, and arrhythmia. The diagnosis was confirmed through cardiac MRI and elevated cardiac biomarkers. Treatment involved immediate cessation of ICI therapy and initiation of high-dose corticosteroids. For patients with inadequate response, additional immunosuppressive agents were considered. This case series presents four cases of late-onset ICI-associated myocarditis, which highlights the importance of long-term surveillance for this potentially fatal complication. Further research is needed to establish optimal treatment strategies and long-term management for this complex condition.
